5 05-02-2026 Re. I.A. No. 01 of 2026: -
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State on this interlocutory application seeking suspension of sentence and release of the appellant on bail during pendency of the appeal.
2. This Court had earlier issued notice to the informant-respondent No.2.
The notice has been duly served upon the informant, but he has chosen not to enter appearance in this case.
3. Records have been placed before this Court to consider the prayer of the appellant for suspension of her Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.834 of 2025(5) dt.05-02-2026 sentence and release on bail during pendency of the appellant.

4. The appellant has been convicted vide judgment dated 12.06.2025 in POCSO Case No. 25 of 2017,
arising out of Bhabhua P.S. Case No. 676 of 2016 dated 01.12.2016, passed by learned Additional Bela Devi vs The State Of Bihar on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39624993/
1 Session Judge VI-cum-Special Judge, POCSO Act, Kaimur, for the offence punishable under Sections 376(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code (for brevity "IPC") and Section 6/17 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (for brevity "POCSO").

sentences.text: By order of sentence dated 20.06.2025, he has been ordered to undergo rigorous imprisonment of twenty years with a fine of Rs.40,000/- for the offence under Sections 6 and 17 of the POCSO Act and in default of payment of fine, he shall further undergo rigorous imprisonment for three years.
For the sake of brevity, punishment under other sections are not mentioned.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the prosecution case is based on the written information furnished by the father of the victim on 01.12.2016.
According to his written information (Exhibit-P-9/P.W.9), his daughter ('X'), aged about 13 years, had left her house in the morning at 09:00 AM for purchase of medicines.
She was going to Bhabhua by a bicycle.
He has not stated anything more than this with regard to what happened after 25.11.2016, but has made a statement that Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.834 of 2025(5) dt.05-02-2026 on 01.12.2016, he saw his daughter together with Guddu Kumar, son of Shri Hitlal Singh of village Gawai,
P.S.-Bhabhua, District-Kaimur.
He alleged that on seeing him, the said Guddu Kumar fled away leaving his daughter.

His daughter started weeping and told him that Guddu Kumar and Chandan Kumar had forcibly taken her to their house, where Hitlal Singh and mother of Guddu had confined her in a room and they wanted to get her married with Chandan Kumar.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that from the FIR itself, it is evident that from 25.11.2016, the victim was missing as she had not returned her home, but no information in this regard was given to the police station.
The informant (P.W.3) has stated in his deposition that his daughter returned after six days.
Nothing has come to explain as to why for six days no information was given to police.
7. Learned counsel further submits that the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., wherein she has stated that she has studied up to class 10th.

On 25th November,
2016, she had reached Bhabhua, where Guddu had given her a phone call and told her to come.
He also told her that he would arrange her marriage with Chandan, who happen to be the younger brother of Guddu.
She has stated that when she reached Bhabhua Nagarpalika, Chandan was not present Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.834 of 2025(5) dt.05-02-2026 there and it was Guddu who confined her for a night, whereafter mother of Guddu asked him to bring her at home, then Guddu took her to his house at Belwatia where she was kept for three days.

She has further stated that when her mother and father came with police in Gawai Mohalla, then she was kept in Nagarpalika for three days, but later on, when he had gone outside, she came out of the house in a bush and took a mobile from a person whereafter she made a call to her mother, thereafter her mother came with the thana people.

8. Learned counsel further submits that in complete contrast to her statement under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C., in her deposition in course of trial, after a year, the victim made several contradictory statements saying that she was subjected to rape by Guddu and Chandan.
She has, however, not alleged any role of the appellant.
It is submitted that from the evidence of her father (P.W.3), it would appear that he has given a completely different version in his deposition.

While he has stated Bela Devi vs The State Of Bihar on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39624993/
2 that he saw the victim in the company of Guddu in the Nagarpalika, who left her after seeing him,
the victim has stated that her mother came with the thana people in the house.

sentences.text: Drastic contradictory statements have been made by P.W. 3 and by no stretch of imagination she can be said to be sterling witness.

9. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.834 of 2025(5) dt.05-02-2026 has opposed the prayer, but has not contested the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that the present appellant, being mother of Guddu and Chandan, has not played any role either in bringing the victim to the Nagarpalika or Gawai Mohalla.
There is no evidence that she had facilitated commission of rape as alleged at a belated stage by the victim.
The medical evidence shows that the victim was between 16-18 years at the time of occurrence.
10. Having regard to the entire facts and circumstances and the evidence which we have prima-facie gone through, at this stage, we find that this appellant is the mother of Guddu and Chandan.
She has not been attributed any role in bringing of the victim girl or in commission of any sexual act with her.

The first statement of the victim is that she had herself come to Bhabhua on asking of Guddu,
who had assured her that she would be married to Chandan, this clearly demonstrates that the victim had gone on her own and she wanted to marry Chandan.
For six days, no information was given to police and this Court has further noticed that there are vacillating statements of the victim which will not put her in the category of the sterling witness.
11. In view of the entire material on record, we find that the appellant has made out a case for suspension of her Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.834 of 2025(5) dt.05-02-2026 sentence and release on bail during pendency of the appeal.

Accordingly, we direct that the sentence of the appellant be suspended and she be released on bail, during pendency of the appeal, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Session Judge-VI-cum- Special Judge, POCSO Act,
Kaimur, in POCSO Case No. 25 of 2017 arising out of Bhabhua P.S. Case No. 676 of 2016.
12. The fine, if any, imposed as a part of sentence shall remain suspended during pendency of the appeal.

13. It is clarified that the observations made hereinabove are only prima-facie and tentative in nature for purpose of consideration of prayer for suspension of sentence and bail of the appellant,
which would not cause prejudice to either of the parties.
14. Interlocutory Application stands disposed of.

15. List this appeal for hearing on its turn.
